subject: Sunrise procurement: PO/invoice requirements and term negotiation
messages:
From: Megan Turner <megan.turner@sunrisehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Procurement: PO requirements and billing cadence for Redwood deployment

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Sunrise is preparing for a phased rollout and procurement needs to confirm billing and PO requirements before we can onboard Redwood as a vendor. A few items we need you to confirm:

- We require a master/blanket PO that references the Master Services Agreement and a PO number on every invoice.
- Standard payment term for suppliers is Net60. We only grant Net30 in exceptional cases with VP/Finance approval.
- Monthly consolidated invoices by legal entity are preferred. Each invoice must include line-item detail and BU charge codes (we will provide chartstring info).
- Vendor onboarding forms (W-9/tax ID, remittance address) are required to complete the vendor record.
- Ability to split invoices by internal BU if the PO covers multiple business units — please confirm format.

I've attached our standard PO template and the vendor setup checklist for your team. Can you confirm whether Redwood is able to accept Net60 and the PO format before we issue a formal PO? Also let me know the contact in your finance team for vendor setup.

Appreciate it — aiming to get procurement sign-off this week.

Best,
Megan Turner
Sr. Procurement Manager
Sunrise Health Systems
Attachment: Sunrise_PO_Template.pdf (pdf)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Megan Turner <megan.turner@sunrisehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Procurement: PO requirements and billing cadence for Redwood deployment

Hi Megan — thanks for the clear list and the template. Looping in Marissa (AE) and Vivek (finance lead) so we can align quickly. A few clarifying points from our side: 

- Redwood’s default public terms are Net30, but we can support Net60 at the enterprise level with a committed annual spend tier. Can you share the expected 12‑month consumption profile (or ballpark ARR) so we can map to discounts/term concessions?
- We can include the PO number on every invoice and produce monthly consolidated invoices with line-item detail. We typically provide one consolidated invoice per legal entity; splitting by BU is doable if you provide the BU codes you mentioned.
- For vendor onboarding we require a completed W-9 (attached) and the remittance address. Our finance email is ap@redwood.com (with Vivek copied) for intake.

Attachments: Redwood_W9.pdf (pdf) — I’ve attached our form to speed things up.

Quick ask: would Sunrise consider a committed spend or pre-pay structure in exchange for earlier payment terms or a larger discount? If you can provide expected volumes we’ll run pricing scenarios and come back with a recommended packaging option.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: Megan Turner <megan.turner@sunrisehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@sunrisehealth.com>, AP <ap@sunrisehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Procurement: PO requirements and billing cadence for Redwood deployment

Jordan — thanks for the quick reply and W-9. A couple of answers from procurement/finance:

- Sunrise policy is Net60 by default. Exceptions require executive approval and are rare; finance will only consider earlier terms for multi-year commitments or if an early-pay discount is offered.
- The preliminary 12‑month consumption for the initial rollout across three BUs is estimated at $320,000. We can tighten estimates after pilot.
- AP contact for processing and vendor upload: ap@sunrisehealth.com (cc’d). Please forward all vendor documents there.
- We need invoice line items to include: Service description, start/end dates of usage, unit quantity (tokens/minutes or seats), rate, BU charge code, and PO number.

I’ve attached our completed vendor setup form and the completed PO template (we haven’t filled in the PO number yet). If Redwood can propose a pricing/packaging option that maps to the $320k estimate and outlines term/discount tradeoffs (e.g., 12‑month committed vs month-to-month), procurement can route it for faster approval.

Thanks — Megan
Megan Turner
Sr. Procurement Manager
Sunrise Health Systems
Attachment: Sunrise_Vendor_Setup_Form.pdf (pdf)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 14:40:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Procurement: PO requirements and billing cadence — pricing options to propose

Team — quick internal note before I respond to Megan with pricing: based on the $320k 12‑month estimate there are two practical packaging options we should surface: 

Option A — Committed Enterprise (preferred):
- 12‑month committed spend of $300k+
- 15% enterprise discount off list rates
- Net30 payment terms
- Monthly consolidated invoices with BU line-items (Redwood handles mapping)

Option B — Flexible Standard:
- Month-to-month or low-commit (no prepay) mapped to $320k projected usage
- 10% discount (intro enterprise pricing)
- Net60 standard (as procurement requires)
- Monthly consolidated invoices; can split by BU on request (may require extra metadata fee)

I recommend offering Option B as the baseline to keep procurement moving and present Option A as an uplift that requires sign-off from the buyer’s finance team. If procurement pushes for Net60 only, we can accept Net60 on Option B with a smaller discount; if they sign to Option A we can make Net30 the default.

Marissa — feel free to adapt this language and share the rate card for DL-2026-0042. Vivek — can you confirm whether the metadata fee for BU-level split invoicing is $750/month? If so we should include it.

—Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Megan Turner <megan.turner@sunrisehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, AP <ap@sunrisehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Procurement: PO requirements and billing cadence for Redwood deployment

Megan — thanks for the estimate and the vendor form. We’ve reviewed internally and can move forward with a pragmatic path to get vendor setup completed this week so you can issue a PO. Summary / commitments from Redwood: 

- Terms / discount: Redwood can accept Net60 for the first 12‑month term under the flexible standard package (Option B) and provide a 10% discount against our standard pricing based on the $320k projected consumption (deal id DL-2026-0042). If Sunrise moves to a 12‑month committed spend of $300k+ we can upgrade to 15% and Net30.
- Invoicing: We will produce monthly consolidated invoices per legal entity. Each invoice will include the PO number, service description, usage start/end dates, unit quantity, rate, and the BU charge code you provide. We can also split invoices by BU on request; there is a metadata processing fee of $750/month for per-BU invoice splits (confirmable).
- Vendor setup: We attached Redwood_W9.pdf earlier; additionally attaching an invoice template and a short MSA amendment that adds a PO‑reference clause to make the process explicit. Please forward the completed vendor form to ap@redwood.com so our finance team can complete onboarding.

Attachments: Invoice_Template_Sunrise.xlsx (xlsx), MSA_amend_redwood_PO_clause.pdf (pdf)

Next steps: 1) Please send the formal PO referencing DL-2026-0042 and indicate whether you want per-BU split invoices; 2) AP to confirm vendor upload and expected payment cycle; 3) Marissa will follow up with formal quote and rate card to align discount math.

Happy to hop on a 20-minute call if procurement prefers to iron out the PO fields live.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
